title: Gas laws
prompt: a glass cylinder of gas with a weighted piston, a thermometer, a pressure gauge and a bunsen burner under it: push the piston down and watch pressure rise as volume falls, light the burner and watch the molecules speed up and the piston rise, pump in more gas; molecules visibly bounce off the walls and piston; stats show P, V, T and PV/T staying constant
blurb: Load, heat and fill a glass piston chamber to explore an ideal gas; PV/T stays constant for fixed gas amount and rises when the pump adds air.
modelNotes: Quasi-static ideal gas with controlled temperature and negligible piston friction. Molecules and instrument response are illustrative. P is absolute, T is kelvin and PV/T equals nR. Pumping increases n, so PV/T cannot remain constant during that action.
